title: ISic004437. Votive dedication of the ruler of Gela, reinscribed by Polyzalos
body:
Text encoding: Valentina Mignosa
1[[[---] Γέλας ἀνέ[θ]ε̄κε [ϝ]ανάσσ[ο̄ν]]]\[Π]ολύζαλός μ’ ἀνέθηκ[ε]/
2[--- τ]ὸν ἄεξ’ εὐο̄́νυμ’ Ἄπολλ̣[ον]

l.1 del Γέλας ἀνέθε̄κε ϝανάσσο̄ν

Text encoding: Valentina Mignosa
1[[[---]ΓΕΛΑΣΑΝΕ[.]Ε̄ΚΕ[.]ΑΝΑΣΣ[...]]]\[.]ΟΛΥΖΑΛΟΣΜΑΝΕΘΗΚ[.]/
2[---.]ΟΝΑΕΞΕΥΟ̄ΝΥΜΑΠΟΛ.[..]

l.1 del Γέλας ἀνέθε̄κε ϝανάσσο̄ν

Facsimile Images

Apparatus criticus

  • Text: Adornato 2008, 33, fig. 3, after Keramopoullos 1909. The text erased on line 1 and the later text cut over it are encoded together; line 2 belongs to both versions.

English translation

Valentina Mignosa

Earlier version: “[...] he, being ruler of Gela, dedicated. [...] Give him glory, noble Apollo.”

Later version: “Polyzalos dedicated me. [...] Give him glory, noble Apollo.” (Adornato)

commentary

The first line originally named a Γέλας ἀνάσσων (“ruler of Gela”) as dedicant. It was subsequently erased and overwritten with the name of Polyzalos, while the second line was left unchanged. Adornato considers the identification of the first dedicant with Polyzalos highly improbable and regards Hieron, ruler of Gela from 485 to 478 BCE, as the likelier candidate, although Gelon cannot be excluded on palaeographic grounds alone.

Adornato dates the first inscription to a period slightly later than Gelon's Delphic tripod base and the recutting by Polyzalos before 466/5 BCE, possibly soon after Hieron's death. He argues that base 3517 and the bronze Charioteer did not belong to the same votive monument.

bibliography

  • Dubois 1989 133 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10000187
  • 1990 40.0427 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10000796
  • Adornato 2008 29-55, especially 32-37 and 50-53
Lines 1-2 (original inscription)

Geloan-Agrigentine western alphabet, with semilunate gamma, four-stroke epsilon and eastern-style xi.

Line 1 (reinscription by Polyzalos)

Later lettering, with eta, three-stroke epsilon, upsilon with a lower vertical stroke, regularised nu and broad mu.
